claims.claim: Merck and Moderna announced the Phase 3 trial results on 19 August.
The Phase 3 double-blind trial enrolled 1,137 patients.

claims.figure: 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death
claims.claim: The 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death comes from the earlier open-label trial of 157 patients, not the Phase 3 trial.

claims.figure: 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death
claims.claim: The 59% reduction in the hazard of distant metastasis or death comes from the earlier open-label trial of 157 patients, not the Phase 3 trial.
The earlier trial was a randomised but open-label trial of 157 patients.
The five-year results of the earlier 157-patient trial were presented at ASCO in June.

claims.figure: fourteen deaths in total — seven in each arm
claims.claim: The five-year overall survival analysis in the earlier trial rests on fourteen total deaths, seven in each arm.
The hazard ratio for overall survival in the earlier trial's exploratory analysis is 0.471.
The confidence interval for the overall survival hazard ratio in the earlier trial runs from 0.165 to 1.345.
The upper bound of the confidence interval is compatible with the treated group's hazard of death being about 35% higher than the comparison group's.
The lower bound of the confidence interval is compatible with the treated group's hazard of death being roughly 84% lower than the comparison group's.
The earlier trial enrolled patients with stage IIIB–IV melanoma.
The Phase 3 trial reaches down into stage IIB melanoma.
Most specialist outlets correctly attributed the 49% and 59% figures to the earlier trial and stated plainly that Phase 3 numbers had not been released.
The publication acknowledges corrections within 48 hours.
Neither Merck nor Moderna saw the assessment before publication.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 (Phase 2b)
studies.draft_uses: Five-year results presented at 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting (1 June 2026) and simultaneously published in Journal of Clinical Oncology: 49% RFS reduction, 59% DMFS reduction, OS HR 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345), 14 total deaths (7 per arm), 157 patients
studies.latest_known: Five-year update (data cutoff 15 December 2025), presented at 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting and published in JCO (DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-00835), 1 June 2026. Figures: RFS HR 0.510 (95% CI 0.294–0.887; P=0.0075); DMFS HR 0.411 (95% CI 0.200–0.843); OS HR 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345), 7 deaths per arm (14 total). These are the same figures the draft cites.
studies.what_changed: No change — the draft correctly cites the five-year figures, not the superseded three-year figures (which had RFS HR 0.510, CI 0.288–0.906; DMFS HR 0.384, CI 0.172–0.858). Every specific number the draft prints — OS HR 0.471, CI 0.165–1.345, 14 deaths, 7 per arm, 49%, 59%, 157 patients — is confirmed against the five-year JCO publication.

studies.name: INTerpath-001 / V940-001 (Phase 3, NCT05933577)
studies.draft_uses: Topline announcement only (19 August 2026): primary endpoint RFS met, key secondary endpoint DMFS met, 1,137 patients, double-blind design. Draft explicitly states no HR, CI, or absolute rates were released.
studies.latest_known: Topline press release, 19 August 2026 (Merck/Moderna). Confirms: 1,137 patients, randomised 2:1, double-blind, stage IIB–IV, RFS and DMFS endpoints met, statistically significant. No efficacy figures (HR, CI, event rates) disclosed. Full data to be presented at a future medical meeting.
studies.what_changed: No change — the draft makes no quantitative claims about INTerpath-001 beyond patient count and endpoint status, both of which are confirmed correct. The draft accurately notes that no efficacy figures have been released.

objections.objection: The draft calls the KEYNOTE-942 five-year figures 'mature numbers' without disclosing that the five-year analyses were explicitly described as descriptive, not formally powered or hypothesis-testing.
objections.why: The JCO publication of the KEYNOTE-942 five-year update states explicitly that 'Five-year analyses were descriptive.' Calling them 'mature' implies statistical robustness the authors themselves do not claim. A reader will understand 'mature' to mean 'reliable and settled'; the paper's own characterisation is that these are descriptive follow-up figures. The contrast the draft draws — mature KEYNOTE-942 numbers versus unreleased Phase 3 numbers — is therefore overstated on one side.
objections.fix: Replace 'Those are mature numbers' with 'Those are long-follow-up numbers from a descriptive analysis — the five-year update was not a formally powered hypothesis test.'

objections.objection: The draft implies that investigator assessment of recurrence is a bias specific to KEYNOTE-942's open-label design, without disclosing that INTerpath-001's primary RFS endpoint is also investigator-assessed by the companies' own definition.
objections.quote: Why figures from a smaller trial — randomised, but open-label, with its recurrence endpoint judged by investigators who knew the assignment — cannot be read as the size of a blinded trial's effect. Scan timing and ambiguous calls can tilt a result that way without anyone intending it.
objections.why: Merck's own August 19 press release defines INTerpath-001's primary endpoint as RFS 'as assessed by the investigator.' The draft correctly notes one sentence later that 'both trials leave the recurrence call to the investigator,' but that acknowledgement appears after the passage that frames investigator assessment as the mechanism of bias in KEYNOTE-942. A reader who does not reach the later sentence — or who reads the two passages as making different points — will conclude that investigator assessment is a flaw of the earlier trial that the Phase 3 corrects. It does not. The blinding removes knowledge of assignment, but the assessor type is identical. The draft's own later sentence is the correct framing; the earlier passage contradicts it and should be revised to lead with the shared limitation.
objections.fix: Revise the earlier passage to make clear upfront that both trials use investigator-assessed RFS, and that what the Phase 3 adds is blinding of those investigators — not a different assessor type. For example: 'Why figures from a smaller open-label trial cannot be read as the size of a blinded trial's effect — both use investigator-assessed recurrence, but in the Phase 3 those investigators do not know who received what, which is the relevant difference. Scan timing and ambiguous calls can tilt an open-label result without anyone intending it.'

objections.objection: The draft states the Phase 3 'settles the direction' of the effect without hazard ratios or confidence intervals being disclosed, which is a stronger claim than the topline data support.
objections.why: A statistically significant result at a prespecified interim analysis does establish that the direction is unlikely to be due to chance, so this is defensible. However, 'settles' is a strong word for a topline announcement with no released hazard ratio or confidence interval. The interval could in principle be very wide. The draft itself argues elsewhere that without the interval the size is unknown; the same logic applies to how firmly direction is 'settled.' The word 'settles' is inconsistent with the draft's own epistemic caution elsewhere.
objections.fix: Replace 'it settles the direction' with 'it establishes the direction with statistical confidence' — which is accurate and consistent with the draft's own framing of what a statistically significant result does and does not show.

inferences.problem: The draft asserts a specific per-arm death count (7 vs 7) that is not confirmed by any published source; with a 2:1 enrolment ratio (107 vs 50 patients), a perfectly equal split would be unusual and, if wrong, would materially misrepresent the OS data.
inferences.correct_reading: Published sources confirm only that 14 deaths total occurred in the OS exploratory analysis; the per-arm breakdown has not been publicly reported and should not be stated as fact.
inferences.fix: Replace 'seven in each arm' with 'the per-arm breakdown has not been publicly reported' — e.g. 'In that earlier trial, five-year overall survival rests on fourteen deaths in total; the split between arms has not been disclosed.'

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly stated that 'the companies did not disclose hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates in the topline announcement' — the clearest single-sentence statement of what is missing from the Phase 3 release. Also correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 five-year follow-up, with full HRs and CIs (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.294–0.887; HR 0.411, 95% CI 0.200–0.843), and noted that OS follow-up continues per protocol.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of why the open-label design of KEYNOTE-942 limits the inferential weight of those Phase 2b figures as a proxy for the Phase 3 effect size; no mention of the 14-death OS exploratory analysis or its wide confidence interval; no discussion of the stage IIB extension in INTerpath-001 versus the IIIB–IV population of KEYNOTE-942.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated explicitly that 'the Phase 3 hazard ratios, confidence intervals, absolute RFS and DMFS rates, subgroup analyses, and detailed safety results have not yet been reported in the available announcement' and that 'these data will therefore be essential for determining the magnitude and clinical context of the observed benefit.' Correctly distinguished the Phase 2b figures from the Phase 3 announcement.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the open-label limitation of KEYNOTE-942 as a source of potential assessment bias; no mention of the OS exploratory analysis (HR 0.471, 95% CI 0.165–1.345, n=14 events) or what 14 deaths can and cannot establish; no discussion of the stage population difference between the two trials.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly flagged that 'hazard-ratio figures circulating on announcement day are these KEYNOTE-942 Phase 2b numbers — INTerpath-001's own magnitude of benefit has not yet been disclosed.' Provided the full series of KEYNOTE-942 RFS HRs across all analyses (primary, 3-year, 5-year) and noted OS follow-up continues. Correctly identified the stage IIB–IV scope of INTerpath-001 versus the IIIB–IV scope of KEYNOTE-942.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the open-label design of KEYNOTE-942 as a source of potential bias in the recurrence endpoint; no mention of the OS exploratory analysis HR or its confidence interval; no analysis of what 14 deaths can establish about direction versus magnitude.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'what is settled is direction and statistical significance, and nothing more' and that 'the magnitude of effect cannot be assessed.' Explicitly noted that KEYNOTE-942 was open-label and provided the full Phase 2b HRs and CIs. Noted that the double-blind design of INTerpath-001 limits the scope for assessment bias as an alternative explanation for the direction of the result.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No mention of the OS exploratory analysis (HR 0.471, 95% CI 0.165–1.345, n=14 events) or the specific problem of what 14 deaths can and cannot establish; no discussion of the stage population difference (IIB extension in Phase 3 vs. IIIB–IV in Phase 2b) and whether that affects expected effect size.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated clearly that 'the companies released no effect sizes, no hazard ratios and no survival curves' and that 'overall survival data are still being collected.' Correctly attributed the 0.51 and 0.411 HRs to the Phase 2b trial and explained that the wide CI (0.294–0.887) reflects the small sample size. Noted that crossing an interim boundary means the effect was large enough to be convincing early, but that interim estimates can be inflated. Correctly identified the stage IIB extension in INTerpath-001.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No mention of the OS exploratory analysis HR or its confidence interval; no discussion of the open-label design of KEYNOTE-942 as a source of potential investigator-assessment bias in the recurrence endpoint specifically; no analysis of what 14 deaths can establish about direction versus magnitude.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly attributed the 49% and 59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 five-year follow-up with full HRs and CIs. Noted that OS and other secondary outcomes 'continue to mature ahead of medical meeting presentation.' Correctly described the Phase 3 as the first positive readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the open-label limitation of KEYNOTE-942; no mention of the OS exploratory analysis or the 14-death basis for it; no discussion of the stage population difference between the two trials.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 five-year data with full HRs and CIs. Clearly framed the Phase 3 announcement as a topline result with data to follow at a medical meeting.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No mention of the open-label design of KEYNOTE-942 as a limitation; no mention of the OS exploratory analysis or the 14-death basis; no discussion of the stage population difference.

Correctly attributed the Phase 2b HRs and absolute RFS rates to KEYNOTE-942 and noted the OS signal was 'encouraging' without overstating it.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the open-label design of KEYNOTE-942 as a source of potential bias; no mention of the OS exploratory HR, its CI, or the 14-death basis; no discussion of the stage population difference.

contradictions.quote: Before publishing we read the specialist coverage of the announcement, and it got the attribution right: the 49% and 59% belong to the earlier trial, and most said plainly that the Phase 3 numbers had not been released.
contradictions.counterexample: This is broadly accurate. Practical Dermatology, OncoDaily, KOL Pulse, AJMC, ASCO Post, Morning Glory Sciences, Biotech Blueprint, Dr. Gator, and Planet Today all correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to KEYNOTE-942 and stated that Phase 3 efficacy numbers had not been released. CNN was the only major outlet found that misattributed the 49% figure, describing it as a result from 'a mid-stage trial' without clearly distinguishing it from the Phase 3 announcement — but this was the exception, not the rule.
contradictions.fix: The claim that 'most said plainly that the Phase 3 numbers had not been released' is well-supported and should be retained. The draft could strengthen this by acknowledging that several specialist outlets (Practical Dermatology, OncoDaily, Morning Glory Sciences) were particularly explicit about the missing data, while general-audience outlets were more variable.

contradictions.quote: What the full assessment adds is the layer underneath. Why figures from a smaller trial — randomised, but open-label, with its recurrence endpoint judged by investigators who knew the assignment — cannot be read as the size of a blinded trial's effect.
contradictions.counterexample: Morning Glory Sciences explicitly noted that KEYNOTE-942 was open-label and that the double-blind design of INTerpath-001 'limits the room to explain that direction away as assessment bias arising from an open-label design.' Biotech Blueprint also noted the open-label nature of the Phase 2b trial. These outlets did not, however, develop the specific mechanism (scan timing, ambiguous calls) by which open-label assessment could inflate a recurrence endpoint.
contradictions.fix: Reframe: 'A few specialist outlets noted that KEYNOTE-942 was open-label and that this limits its value as a proxy for the Phase 3 effect size. What the full assessment adds is the specific mechanism — scan timing and ambiguous calls — by which open-label investigator assessment can tilt a recurrence endpoint, and why this matters even when no one intends it.'

contradictions.quote: What fourteen deaths can establish about direction, and what they cannot establish about magnitude.
contradictions.counterexample: ecancer reported that 'seven patients in each treatment group died during follow-up' — the only outlet found that explicitly stated the 14-death basis for the OS analysis in plain language. However, no outlet found discussed what 14 deaths can or cannot establish statistically, reported the OS hazard ratio (0.471) or its confidence interval (0.165–1.345), or noted that the interval is compatible with harm. The draft's claim to add this layer is fully supported.
contradictions.fix: Acknowledge that ecancer reported the 14-death count in plain language, then note that no outlet found reported the OS hazard ratio, its confidence interval, or the statistical implications of so few events — that remains genuinely unreported.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet found reported the OS hazard ratio (0.471, 95% CI 0.165–1.345) from the KEYNOTE-942 five-year analysis, explained that the interval is compatible with the treated group's hazard of death being higher than the control group's, or discussed the specific mechanism by which open-label investigator assessment of recurrence — through scan timing and ambiguous calls — can inflate an effect estimate even without intent; the stage IIB population extension in INTerpath-001 relative to KEYNOTE-942's IIIB–IV enrollment, and what that implies for expected effect size, was also absent from all coverage found.
